source.title: Decoding-Unlearning: Fact Forgetting via Entropy-Guided Inference
source.authors: Jingwen Pu; Ming-Jun Shi; Xinrui Ren; Yizhen Wang; Xinyu Zhang; Zhao-Kun Wang; Kun She

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates its own inference-time unlearning method and tests whether rephrased queries defeat it, using different methods and measures from the parameter-editing unlearning approaches in the claim.
record.gate_note: The main benchmark tables report SEGUE's unlearning and utility outcomes. The directly relevant recovery-style test is the semantic-drift experiment on rephrased MUSE-Books queries; the paper does not test recovery by fine-tuning, activation ablation, quantization, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information. Probe decision accuracy is not itself a measurement of recovered target knowledge.
record.test_reason: The study proposes SEGUE, a training-free decoding-time unlearning method. It evaluates it against prompt-based extraction: RWKU adversarial-attack probes and GPT-4o obscure rephrasing of MUSE-Books. That bears on Version F (a newer method resisting attacks), not tested with the original attack recipes. The other rows only report SEGUE's own forgetting and utility numbers with no attack, so they do not test the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also claim SEGUE outperforms most existing inference-time (and some training-based) baselines while being far cheaper in time and memory. They present robustness to adversarial prompts (RWKU AA) and semantic rephrasing as evidence of strong robustness.
record.recipe_differences: SEGUE is a training-free inference-time decoding intervention using a probe, entropy-guided token selection, hard masking, and smooth logit decay; it does not update model weights.
record.method_sensitivity: The semantic-drift result depends on the backbone understanding the rephrased query: the authors state that when it does not activate the factual knowledge, the probe outputs “No” and no unlearning intervention is applied. SEGUE's informative layer and β are model-specific; hard-mask strength k and smooth-decay strength α are also studied as parameters.
record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL 2026)
record.problems: The directly relevant robustness test covers one rephrased dataset and does not evaluate the other recovery attacks in the claim. The paper reports no uncertainty estimates for these results. The rephrasing table does not state the backbone model. The paper itself notes that its copyright-task evaluation data are relatively limited and focuses on single-turn, short-text generation.
record.rows_left_out: No other directly relevant recovery-attack results were reported. Other tables compare SEGUE and baselines on unlearning efficacy, utility, probe performance, and computational costs; probe decision accuracy and unrelated ablations do not measure recovered target knowledge.

untested.parts: No fine-tuning or relearning attack, no activation ablation, no quantization, no other-language queries, no in-context-information attack, and no dedicated jailbreak suite beyond RWKU's adversarial probes. The probe could also be bypassed by queries it misclassifies, and this is not tested adversarially.
Not tested on weight-based unlearned models as a recovery attack, except incidentally through the baselines' RWKU AA scores (see missing).
No test of whether a weight-editing method's forgetting survives simple attacks.
Not tested. SEGUE blocks access at decoding by design rather than deleting knowledge, but this is a design property, not a finding.

missing.what: SEGUE on RWKU adversarial-attack (AA) probes: Llama-2-7B 4.21 vs original 50.26 (Table 1); Llama-3-8B 5.71 vs 76.09 and Qwen2.5-14B 4.88 vs 44.33 (Table 4).

Baseline unlearning methods under RWKU AA vs plain QA on Llama-2-7B. LLMU keeps 34.51/54.55 on QA but 42.45/50.26 on AA; NPO keeps 19.75/54.55 on QA but 27.93/50.26 on AA. Adversarial probes extract relatively more retained knowledge from weight-based methods. The study does not frame this as recovery.
WMDP accuracy near chance under SEGUE with MMLU nearly kept (Llama-2-7B Bio 28.36, Chem 22.30, Cyber 23.05, Gen 42.85 vs 44.47). This is efficacy only, with no attack.

record.verdict_notes: SEGUE does not change weights; the knowledge stays in the model and is suppressed at decoding when a prompt-based probe fires. So it is a guardrail-style counter-method, and its robustness claims cover only prompt-level attacks. Attacks that bypass the decoding wrapper, such as running the raw weights, are trivially out of scope. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The original sources are not this study.

versions.untested_parts: No broad attack suite; no fine-tuning recovery, activation ablation, or quantization. The unlearning and utility measurements use ROUGE-L and MMLU rather than a stated chance-level accuracy criterion.
No recovery fine-tuning on unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten-fact examples.
No activation-direction ablation or test of whether an unlearning method blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
No low-bit quantization of unlearned weights.
Tests semantic rephrasing on MUSE-Books only; does not test jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
SEGUE is evaluated against semantic rephrasing only; resistance to fine-tuning, internal edits, quantization, jailbreaks, other languages, and in-context information is not tested.

rows.note: The paper says the probe remains accurate when the backbone understands the rephrased query; the reported SEGUE score does not show recovery of the target response. The model identity and the exact relation between the Original and SEGUE figures are not stated.
rows.check: This is the counter-method's result under a rephrasing attack, so it belongs to F, not E. E concerns recovery from unlearned models; one guardrail resisting rephrasing is evidence for F. The baseline 23.13 is the original model's score on the rephrased queries, already far below its 98.21 on plain queries, so the attack weakens the original model too. The backbone is not stated; presumably ICLM-7B.

relation.reason: The study evaluates its own counter-method under rephrasing and RWKU adversarial-attack probes, which bears on F.

tranche.reason: SEGUE is a different method (training-free decoding-time unlearning) aimed at the same question. It is tested under prompt attacks: RWKU AA and GPT-4o obscure rephrasing.

source_check.notes: The rephrasing test is one GPT-4o-rephrased MUSE-Books set with no model named. Rephrasing alone drops the original model from 98.21 (Table 2, ICLM-7B) to 23.13, so the attack is weak. SEGUE leaves weights unchanged; fine-tuning, quantization and weight-access attacks are untested. The r5 citations in all three pack statements are spurious.

statements.correction: This study: SEGUE (training-free, decoding-time, weights unchanged; ACL 2026). Perf 4.28 on GPT-4o obscurely rephrased MUSE-Books vs 23.13 for the original model, probe accuracy 95%, backbone not stated (Table 13). RWKU AA 4.21, 5.71, 4.88 vs original 50.26, 76.09, 44.33 on Llama-2-7B, Llama-3-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-14B (Tables 1, 4).
statements.problem: It cites r5 but says nothing about SEGUE: it covers only NSRU, NEDS, AdaPop and RULE. Its conditions (weight-updating methods; WMDP/TOFU/DUET; 'All four are preprints') do not fit this peer-reviewed MUSE-Books/RWKU study.

statements.correction: This study: SEGUE (frozen weights; probe plus entropy-guided decoding). Perf 4.28 on obscurely rephrased MUSE-Books vs 23.13 for the original model, probe accuracy 95%, backbone not stated (Table 13). RWKU AA 4.21, 5.71, 4.88 vs original 50.26, 76.09, 44.33 on Llama-2-7B, Llama-3-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-14B.
statements.problem: It cites r5 but says nothing about SEGUE: it covers only ARIA, GUARD-IT, Nullify and ICCU. SEGUE does fit the frozen-weights, added-component category, but its benchmark (MUSE-Books, RWKU) and models are not listed.

statements.correction: This study: SEGUE Perf 4.28 on obscurely rephrased MUSE-Books vs 23.13 for the original model (its own direct Books Perf 6.29), probe accuracy 95%. That is resistance, not a challenge to F. Remove r5 from this statement.
statements.problem: This challenges statement cites r5, but r5 shows SEGUE resisting rephrasing. The study has no weight-access, system-access or fine-tuning test, so nothing in it shows resistance holding only under the designed route.
